rv.q: The unshowy way the two lead actresses progress from childhood to old age is a pleasure to behold.
McCormack is magnificent at conveying Lila's misdirected anger – a rage nurtured by years of disappointment, oppression and abuse.
For three-quarters of its running time, I was entertained.
April De Angelis’s adaptation has much to recommend it, ambitious and epic in its reach.
Packed into just over five hours of stage time, it is in danger of seeming to have more width than depth...

cn.t: April De Angelis's adaptation of Elena Ferrante's beloved novel receives mixed reviews, with critics praising the richly textured exploration of female friendship but questioning whether the sprawling story fully succeeds on stage.
